svg.aria-label: An annotated project tree. Each row is a file, with a coloured pill naming the routing rule that applies and, to its right, the URL the file serves or the reason it serves none. Root files proxy.ts and instrumentation.ts sit beside app/. Under app/: the root layout, page and not-found; root-only metadata favicon.ico and robots.ts; a (marketing) group whose about page serves /about and whose opengraph-image.png gets a hash suffix; blog with an ignored card.tsx, a private _lib folder never read by next build, and a [slug] dynamic segment with a page, a loading file that creates no route, and an icon prerendered once at /blog/-/icon.png; a catch-all, an optional catch-all, a %5Fdebug folder serving /_debug, an API route handler; a dashboard with @team and @analytics slots in which @team/settings/page.tsx serves /dashboard/settings; a feed with an @modal slot holding a (..)photo/[id] interception page that serves /photo/:id only when the next-url header is /feed or below; the canonical photo/[id] page; and this post's sec0/a/[id] route serving /sec0/a/1 to /sec0/a/5. An inset shows a pages/ tree in which card.tsx and _lib/data.ts are routes. A legend gives the colour families, and a box states that deleting dashboard/default.tsx or photo/[id]/page.tsx would fail strict route matching, naming the errors each deletion raises.
svg.text: Node.js only; default matcher /:path* runs it on every request
register() runs once per server instance
walked by collectAppFiles, which keeps four kinds of file
root layout: discovered, but no URL of its own
✗ not a convention stem: never an entry
✗ folder skipped before readdir in next build
param slug: string, short code d
no route: looked up when a page's tree is built
children on a hard load of /dashboard/settings; strict needs it
analytics at both URLs; the slot's only file
prop modal on feed/layout; not in the URL
returns null when no modal matches
serves /photo/:id when next-url is /feed or below
INSET · THE SAME IDEA IN PAGES/
every page-extension file is a route candidate.
group, slot: deleted from the URL
convention file with no URL of its own
page: the leaf that makes a URL
As drawn, every URL has a complete tree.
Rows ending in / are folders; guide lines show nesting. A folder name is a URL segment unless its pill says otherwise.
